LD 2076 -An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Reporting of Incidents by Municipal
Fire Chiefs
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the Criminal Justice
and Public Safety Committee, my name is Shawn Esler, and it is a privilege to serve as the State
Fire Marshal.
I am here today to testify in support of LD 2076. This is a technical but important bill that keeps
Maine law aligned with national fire and emergency incident reporting standards. For decades, fire departments have reported incident data using the National Fire Incident Reporting System, or NFIRS. At the federal level, the United States Fire Administration is transitioning to a modernized system known as the National Emergency Response Information System, or NERIS.
LD 2076 provides clear statutory authority for that transition. It allows departments to continue
reporting under NFIRS through January l, 2026, and then requires reporting under NERIS or a
successor system thereafter. This ensures continuity in data collection, avoids disruption for municipalities, and maintains Maine's compliance with federal requirements.
I would also like to note the significant implementation work already underway. Senior Plamier Michelle Mason Webber with the State Fire Marshal's Office has spent the past year ensuring
Maine's NERIS program is ready to go live. Together, we have conducted multiple statewide
webinars and spent hundreds of hours working directly with municipal fire chiefs to answer questions and support departments through the transition.
Accurate incident reporting is essential for fire prevention, emergency planning, firefighter
safety, and federal grant eligibility. LD 2076 does not create new reporting requirements or new
costs for municipalities. The State Fire Marshal's Office already supports and funds a statewide reporting system and will continue to do so.
In short, LD 2076 is a necessary housekeeping bill that supports Maine's fire service and ensures
uninterrupted access to critical incident data.
Thank you for your time, and I would be happy to answer any questions.

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association In Support of
LD 2076, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Reporting of Incidents by Municipal Fire Chiefs
February 9, 2026
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and members of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee, my name is Tanya Emery, and I am providing testimony today in support of LD 2076 at the direction of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). MMA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit member service organization that aims to help provide policy solutions that work for all residents of Maine. The LPC is composed of 70 municipal officials from across Maine, elected by their peers to represent member communities.
From a municipal perspective, clear and consistent reporting requirements are essential. LD 2076 provides needed clarity around incident reporting, helping ensure that data submitted by fire departments is accurate, consistent, and useful at both the local and state levels.
Reliable incident data supports better decision-making, improves public safety planning, and helps municipalities and the State allocate resources more effectively. Importantly, this bill accomplishes these goals without placing unnecessary administrative burdens on local fire departments.
For these reasons, MMA's LPC urges the committee to support LD 2076. Thank you for your time and attention to this matter, and I am happy to answer any questions you might have.
Tanya L. Emery Advocacy Manager, Maine Municipal Association temery@memun.org
